rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the proposed sense lacks contextual connection: if nearness has persisted from the world's beginning through and beyond revelation, an ongoing form would better express it.
rows.anchor: فإن الإقتراب بذلك المعنى مستمر من أول بدء الدنيا إلى يوم نزول الآية بل إلى ما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection says actual nearness is especially apt to the context, since it states the real closeness of the reckoning and threatens the disbelievers who doubt the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: هذا المعنى الذي اعترضه أنسب بما هو مقتضى المقام من إخافة الكفرة اللئام المرتابين في أمر القيام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the reckoning near with God; its critic objects that created things cannot be near or far in relation to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد اقتراب ذلك عند الله تعالى وتعقب بأنه لا عند لله عز وجل إذ لا نسبة للكائنات إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection misunderstands the phrase: nearness with God means the reckoning is in His eternal knowledge or decree, not spatial or temporal proximity to Him.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد من عند الله في علمه الأزلي أو في حكمه وتقديره لا الدنو والإقتراب المعروف

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: A scholar explains nearness by God's perfect forbearance: long human eras are short by His measure, so the remaining time is truly brief and people should prepare.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الأفاضل : ليس المراد من كون القرب عند الله تعالى نسبته إليه سبحانه

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Sheikh al-Islam rejects this reading here because proximity to God cannot change or renew; that consideration suits verses that do not assert an event's temporal occurrence.
rows.anchor: شيخ الإسلام في الإعتراض على ما قيل أنه لا سبيل إلى اعتباره ههنا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another scholar takes nearness with God in its familiar idiomatic sense, as nearness in divine knowledge or decree, with renewal belonging to the relation, as in the raising of the Sleepers.
rows.anchor: اختار بعضهم أن المراد بالعندية ما سمعته أولا وهو معنى شائع في الإستعمال وجعل التجدد باعتبار التعلق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is certain occurrence: whatever is coming is near, while what is distant is what has already passed; a poetic line illustrates the contrast.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد من اقترابه تحقق وقوعه لا محالة فإن كل آت قريب والبعيد ما وقع ومضى

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: A scholar objects that certainty of occurrence does not explain the past-tense verb's implication of nearness unless the form is stripped of its eventive force, as in timeless praise formulas.
rows.anchor: وبعض الأفاضل قال : إنه على هذا الوجه

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Fronting for people hastens the threat: associating the approach with the polytheists at the outset immediately distresses and frightens them.
rows.anchor: للمسارعة إلى إدخال الروعة فإن نسبة الإقتراب إلى المشركين من أول الأمر يسوؤهم ويورثهم رهبة وانزعاجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their heedlessness and turning away do not preclude fear: a warning can unsettle them if they entertain even a remote possibility that it is true.
rows.anchor: في ذهنهم احتمال الصدق ولو مرجوحا

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators report that after the earlier warning that the Hour was near, unbelievers paused some deeds, then mocked its delay; this verse made them fear and wait, but they later resumed mocking.
rows.anchor: قال الكفار فيما بينهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A rhetorician says approach suggests something advancing toward a target; adding for people makes them the pursued party fleeing it, which conveys danger and fear.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم في بيان ذلك : إن الإقتراب منبيء عن التوجه والإقبال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Putting for people before naming the reckoning delays identification of the terrifying approaching thing, letting the hearer imagine its horror; the reverse order would reveal the subject sooner.
rows.anchor: قيل ذكر الحساب بخلاف ما إذا قيل اقترب الحساب للناس فإن كون إقبال الحساب نحوهم لا يفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rationale is the Prophet's established practice of warning the polytheists: fronting for people signals from the start that the discourse concerns them and something distressing.
rows.anchor: إن جريان عادته الكريمة صلى الله عليه وسلم على إنذار المشركين وتحذيرهم وبيان ما يزعجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument relies on the Prophet's habit of speaking distressingly when discussing them, not a claim that most of his speech in all settings is distressing.
rows.anchor: لا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام يتكلم في غالب أحواله بما يسوؤهم وفرق بين العادتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting aims to hasten the warning even if the audience does not in fact feel fear, just as a warning's intended effect remains its purpose when it fails.
rows.anchor: التقديم لتعجيل التخويف ولا ينافي ذلك عدم حصوله كما لا ينافي عدم حصول التخويف كون إنزال الآيات للتخويف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the lām as reinforcing the possessive relation: rather than deleting an annexed noun, the phrase uses a fronted locative predicate, followed by the definite reckoning.
rows.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون اللام تأكيدا لإضافة الحساب إليهم قال في الكهف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says fronting, the explicit lām, and the definite article add emphases absent from the basic wording; with their possessive force the lām reinforces restriction.
rows.anchor: جوز الزمخشري كون اللام تأكيدا لإضافة الحساب إليهم

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Sheikh al-Islam and others criticize al-Zamakhshari's analysis as strained and contrary to the context; other scholars defend it, but the author prefers taking the lām as complement of approach.
rows.anchor: وادعى شيخ الإسلام أنه مع كونه تعسفا تاما بمعزل عما يقتضيه المقام وبحث فيه أيضا أبو حيان وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes the reality of the reckoning; the author says reckoning as recompense is denied only by polytheists.
rows.anchor: استدل بالآية على ثبوت الحساب

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says Mu'tazilites and Kharijites deny the reckoning; al-Nasafi quotes Mu'tazilites denying the balance, reckoning, bridge, pool, and intercession, interpreting such references as justice.
rows.anchor: وذكر البيضاوي في تفسير قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that standard kalam works generally report most Mu'tazilites rejecting the bridge and all rejecting the balance, without mentioning rejection of the reckoning.
rows.anchor: أن أكثرهم بنفي الصراط وجميعهم ينفي الميزان ولم يتعرض فيها لنفيهم الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading confines their profound ignorance to the approaching reckoning, while another includes ignorance of God, revelation, messengers, resurrection, reward, punishment, and all prophetic teaching.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأولى التعميم أي في غفلة تامة وجهالة عامة من توحيده تعالى والإيمان بكتبه ورسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning heedlessness after the reckoning does not restrict it to the reckoning, since their regret and ignorance will become evident on the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: وذكر غفلتهم عن ذلك عقيب بيان اقتراب الحساب لا يقتضي قصر الغفلة عليه فإن وقوع تأسفهم وندامتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that anyone heedless of God's requital commits every kind of error and plunges into every kind of ignorance.
rows.anchor: ومن غفل عن مجازاة الله تعالى له المراد من الحساب صدر منه كل ضلالة وركب متن كل جهالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase belongs to an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بمحذوف واقع خبرا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The turning away is from signs and warnings that call them to saving faith; it is a second predicate alongside their being heedless.
rows.anchor: أي عن الآيات والنذر الناطقة بذلك الداعية إلى الإيمان به المنجي من المهالك خبر بعد خبر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari resolves the apparent tension by making them initially unaware of the outcome, then deliberately averse after warnings awaken them to it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : وصفهم بالغفلة مع الإعراض على معنى

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says their persistent heedlessness concerns rational proofs; when scriptural proofs join them and they are guided to reflection, they turn away.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف أراد أن حالهم المستمرة الغفلة عن مقتضى الأدلة العقلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal clause with a prepositional phrase conveys settled heedlessness, while the participial description of turning away indicates a renewed action; treating both as a single state is weaker.
rows.anchor: وفيه بيان فائدة إيراد الأول جملة ظرفية لما في حرف الظرف من الدلالة على التمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that reason itself requires reward and punishment works only with moral good and evil known by reason, which Ash'arites strongly deny.
rows.anchor: لا يتسنى إلا على القبول بالحسن والقبح العقليين والأشاعرة ينكرون ذلك أشد الإنكار

rows.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
rows.claim: Another scholar allows a sense of being extensive or excessive in heedlessness, supported by Arabic usage and the verse about turning away after rescue to land.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الأفاضل : يمكن أن يحمل الإعراض على الإتساع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heedlessness may also mean neglect, a usage that avoids contradiction between heedlessness and deliberate turning away.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أيضا أن يراد بالغفلة معنى الإهمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement recounts the offense of a group of Khuzāʿa, who claimed the angels were God's daughters; al-Wahidi also attributes the claim to Quraysh and several Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: وهم حي من خزاعة قالوا الملائكة بنات الله سبحانه ونقل الواحدي أن قريشا وبعض العرب جهينة وبني سلامة وخزاعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit Qatada's report that Jews claimed God had intermarried with jinn and angels were born from them; the first account is the famous one.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة قال قالت اليهود إن الله عز وجل صاهر الجن فكانت بينهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns every attribution of offspring to God, including Christians calling Jesus God's son and Jews calling Ezra God's son.
rows.anchor: والآية مشنعة على كل من نسب إليه سبحانه ذلك كالنصارى القائلين عيسى ابن الله واليهود القائلين عزير ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Him the All-Merciful heightens the absurdity, since the title presents everything besides Him as His dependent creature.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الرحمانية المنبئة عن جميع ما سواه تعالى مربوبا له تعالى لإبراز كمال شناعة مقالتهم الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥānah declares God's transcendence in the manner befitting Him; the word may be the verbal noun of glorifying, a name for glorification, or an imperative to glorify Him.
rows.anchor: السبحان مصدر سبح أي بعد أن أسبحه تسبيحة على أنه علم للتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than offspring, the angels are created servants and God's property; the rebuttal argues that offspring cannot themselves be owned.
rows.anchor: بل هم عباد من حيث أنهم مخلوقون له تعالى فهم ملكه سبحانه والولد لا يصح تملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honored means brought near to God, which identifies the source of the mistaken claim about them.
rows.anchor: أي مقربون عنده تعالى تنبيه على منشأ غلطهم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads the word with a doubled rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة مكرمون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means came near; another view says it expresses nearness more emphatically than qaruba.
rows.anchor: أي قرب وقيل هو أبلغ في القرب من قرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise is the resurrection, reckoning, and recompense after the second trumpet blast, rather than the first; the clause follows the opening of Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: ما بعد النفخة الثانية من البعث والحساب والجزاء لا النفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long report in Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah places Gog and Magog after Jesus kills the Dajjal: they die by a divine affliction, then birds and rain cleanse the earth, abundance returns, a wind takes every believer, and the Hour comes upon the wicked.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج مسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه من حديث طويل إن الله تعالى يوحي إلى عيسى عليه السلام بعد أن يقتل الدجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report related by Ahmad and others compares the Hour after Gog and Magog perish to a full-term pregnancy whose delivery surprises the family by night or day.
rows.anchor: وجاء من حديث رواه أحمد وجماعة أن الساعة بعد أن يهلك يأجوج ومأجوج كالحامل المتم لا يدري أهلها حتى تفجأهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the Prophet said that if a horse survived the emergence of Gog and Magog, its foal would not be ridden before the Hour, stressing its nearness.
rows.anchor: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لو نجت فرس عند خروجهم

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer uses surprise إذا, which can replace the linking fāʾ for a nominal clause; using both here strengthens the link.
rows.anchor: وإذا للمفاجأة وهي تسد مسد الفاء الجزائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard parsing makes هي the pronoun of the matter, شاخصة the fronted predicate, and أبصار the delayed subject; the sentence then explains that pronoun.
rows.anchor: والضمير للقصة والشأن وهو مبتدأ و ( شاخصة ) خبر مقدم

rows.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
rows.claim: Some Kufans allow the pronoun of the matter to take a single-word predicate, which would permit شاخصة to be predicate and أبصار its subject; the author rejects this parsing under the usual rule.
rows.anchor: وأجاز بعض الكوفيين كونه مفردا فيجوز ما ذكر عنده

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra takes هي as a pronoun for the eyes, clarified later in its predicate; Ibn Malik and others allow such a pronoun to precede its referent.
rows.anchor: وعن الفراء أن هي ضمير الأبصار فهو ضمير مبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase هو الجد حتى تفضل العين أختها is cited as poetic evidence for a pronoun whose referent follows it.
rows.anchor: هو الجد حتى تفضل العين أختها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows a later clarifier outside the pronoun's predicate when context indicates the referent, citing a line about Malik ibn Abi Ka'b.
rows.anchor: بل نقل عن الفراء أنه متى دل الكلام على المرجح وذكره بعده ما يفسره

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also calls هي a separative or support pronoun and cites poetry; this works only with al-Kisa'i's allowance for placing it before the predicate while the predicate precedes the subject.
rows.anchor: ونقل عنه أيضا أن ( هي ) ضمير فصل وعماد يصلح موضعه

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Tha'labi makes the clause end at فإذا هي, understood as the Hour appearing or occurring, then begins شاخصة أبصار; the author calls this strained and discordant.
rows.anchor: الكلام قد تم عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Another reported parsing makes اقترب the conditional answer and treats the waw as extra, a view attributed to al-Farra in Majma al-Bayan.
rows.anchor: الواو سيف خطيب ونقل ذلك في مجمع البيان عن الفراء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Basran grammarians do not allow an extra waw; they take the answer as an elided saying, يا ويلنا.
rows.anchor: عن الزجاج أن البصريين لا يجوزون زيادة الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If اقترب is taken as the answer, the cry is also introduced by an implicit they-said; يقولون يا ويلنا may be a circumstantial clause or a fresh sentence.
rows.anchor: قدر القول ههنا أيضا وجعله حالا من الموصول يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes stare upward with raised lids and without blinking, from the terror of the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: شخوص الأبصار رفع أجفانها إلى قوق من دون أن تطرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cry for woe expresses regret, as if summoning woe to arrive because its time has come.
rows.anchor: من نداء الويل التحسر وكأنهم قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they had been wholly heedless of the resurrection and return to God for recompense; another view specifies that they did not know this day was real.
rows.anchor: الذي دهمنا من البعث والرجوع إليه عز وجل للجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They retract the claim of heedlessness: warnings had reached them, but they wronged themselves by abandoning or denying the signs and warnings, exposing themselves to eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: ظالمين بترك الآيات والنذر مكذبين بها

words: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse presents proof to silence disputants after warning of their end; people here most likely means unbelievers who dispute and deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: إقامة للحجة التي تلقم المجادلين في البعث حجرا أثر الإشارة إلى ما يؤل إليه أمرهم واستظهر أن المراد بالناس هنا الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their certainty of impossibility mere doubt signals the weakness of their case: even obstinate deniers can only allege doubt against clear evidence; indefinite wording and إن further diminish it.
rows.anchor: وأما الجزم بعدم الإمكان فخارج من دائرة الإحتمال كما أن تنكيره وتصديره بكلمة الشك للإشعار بأن حقه أن يكون ضعيفا مشكون الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording avoids saying directly that they doubt the resurrection: any doubt lies on their side, and the phrase treats them as persistently immersed in it without implying it is strong.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يقل وإن ارتبتم في البعث للمبالغة في تنزيه أمره عن شائبة وقوع الريب والإشعار بأن ذلك إن وقع فمن جهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من is partitive in origin and attaches to an omitted adjective describing doubt; the author prefers doubt about resurrection's possibility, while occurrence is also possible but the following proof only establishes possibility and verse 22:7 already states it will occur.
rows.anchor: ومن ابتدائية متعلقة بمحذوف وقع صفة للريب واستظهر أن المراد في ريب من إمكان البعث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads البعث with a fatḥa on the ʿayn; Basrans treat it as a dialect variant, while Kufans call the usual sukūn a regular lightening of a middle guttural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( من البعث ) بفتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains the conditional answer, or means implicitly: consider your origin and your doubt will vanish; an estimate meaning I will inform you is less apt.
rows.anchor: دليل جواب الشرط أو الجواب بتأويل أي وإن كنتم في ريب من البعث فانظروا إلى مبدأ خلقكم ليزول ريبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's creation from soil means either the creation of Adam from it or the formation of semen from food grown in it; although food includes other elements, soil predominates, and the author prefers the first account.
rows.anchor: وخلقهم من تراب في ضمن خلق آدم عليه السلام منه أو بخلق الأغذية التي يتكون منها المني منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nutfah is a drop, from dripping, and here means the semen from which each individual is immediately created; al-Naqqash's view that it means Adam's semen is exceedingly remote.
rows.anchor: أي مني من النطف بمعنى التقاطر وقال الراغب

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines nutfah as pure water and says it is used for a man's semen; the author replies that the word also denotes semen generally, so the definition does not exclude that usage.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : النطفة الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿalaqah is a formed piece of clotted blood, and a muḍghah is a piece of flesh formed from it, about the size of what can be chewed.
rows.anchor: قطعة من الدم جامدة متكونة من المني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms are genitive adjectives of muḍghah; Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads both in the accusative as circumstantial qualifiers, a rare construction Sibawayh permits by analogy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة بالنصب فيهما على الحال من النكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading means a morsel whose form has become visible and one not yet formed; limbs first remain indistinct, then appear gradually. The unformed state comes second because it is privative, and intensive morphology reflects many separately formed organs.
rows.anchor: أن المخلقة المستبينة الخلق أي مضغة مستبينة الخلق مصورة ومضغة لم يستبن خلقها وصورتها بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another lexical reading takes mukhallaqah as smoothed and free of defect, from verbs meaning to smooth wood or a stone; the opposite has defects, yielding variation in people's forms, stature, and completeness.
rows.anchor: المخلقة المسواة الملساء من النقصان والعيب

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبي العالية وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, al-Sha'bi, Abu al-Aliya, and Ikrima say the formed one completes its term and develops stage by stage, while the unformed one miscarries before term.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد وقتادة والشعبي وأبي العالية وعكرمة أن المخلقة التي تم لها مدة الحمل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that an angel asks God whether the settled semen is to be formed; if so, the angel asks its sex, fortune, lifespan, provision, and place of death. The report is treated as Prophetic.
rows.anchor: عن مسعود قال : النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أخذها ملك الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are described as coming from the kind of semen that completes formation or miscarries, not literally from both kinds, since a miscarried semen does not produce a person; the contrast magnifies divine power.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنهم خلقوا من جنس هذه النطفة الموصوفة بالتامة والساقطة لا أنهم خلقوا من نطفة تامة

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike 23:14, where each stage creates the next, here every stage is a starting point in the creation of human beings, further displaying God's power.
rows.anchor: وفي جعل كل واحدة من هذه المراتب مبدأ لخلقهم لا لخلق ما بعدها من المراتب كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause attaches to خلقنا; its object is omitted for grandeur and breadth, encompassing truths and subtleties beyond enumeration.
rows.anchor: متعلق بخلقنا وترك المفعول لتفخيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gradual creation teaches the reality of resurrection: the one who originated humans from lifeless soil and transformed them through disparate stages can restore them, more easily by analogy.
rows.anchor: فإن من تأمل فيما ذكر من الخلق التدريجي جزم بأن من قدر على خلق البشر أولا من تراب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some specify the omitted object as the matter of resurrection, but the author considers the broader, unstated object better.
rows.anchor: وقدّر بعضهم المفعول خاصا أي لنبين لكم أمر البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects as very far-fetched the claim that the point is to show creation is a choice of the agent, otherwise some embryos would not be formed.
rows.anchor: وأبعد جدا من زعم أن المعنى لنبين لكم أن التخليق اختيار من الفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads ليبين with a third-person yāʾ, an instance of rhetorical shift in person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( ليبين )
